Bulgarian

[edit]
 адмирал and адмирал (пеперуда) on Bulgarian Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From Russian адмира́л (admirál) and German Admiral, from English and Old French admiral, from Medieval Latin admiralis, from Arabic أَمِير (ʔamīr, “commander”) + -alis (“-al”) under influence from admīrārī (“to admire, to respect”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɐdmiˈraɫ]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -aɫ

Noun

[edit]

адмира́л • (admirál) m (relational adjective адмира́лски or адмира́лов)

  1. admiral
  2. flag officer
  3. red admiral (butterfly Vanessa atalanta)

Kumyk

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian адмира́л (admirál), from Dutch admiraal, ultimately from Arabic أمير (“commander”).

Noun

[edit]

адмирал • (admiral)

  1. (military, navy) admiral (naval officer of the highest rank)

  • адмира́лъ (admirál) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

    From Old French admiral etc., from Medieval Latin admiralis etc., from Arabic أَمِير (ʔamīr, “commander”) + -alis (“-al”) under influence from admīrārī (“to admire, to respect”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): [ɐdmʲɪˈraɫ]
    • Audio:(file)
    • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
    • Hyphenation: ад‧ми‧ра́л

    Noun

    [edit]

    адмира́л • (admirál) m anim (genitive адмира́ла, nominative plural адмира́лы, genitive plural адмира́лов, relational adjective адмира́льский)

    1. (military) admiral
    2. red admiral (Vanessa atalanta, butterfly)
